parsed.explanation: The objection is valid: inclusion-minimal transversals of an intersecting family of finite sets can be infinite, as the stated example demonstrates. Claim 3.2 applies π(T) without proving T finite, so it does not establish the self-duality hypothesis used in Step 4 for arbitrary minimal transversals. This gap resurfaces when Zorn produces a minimal transversal inside I∪Z_ω, which need not be finite. Since the finiteness conclusion rests on that unproved self-duality, the required finiteness/large-prime-erasure statement L6.2 is not established elsewhere. Repair requires a substantive lemma ruling out or otherwise handling infinite minimal transversals.
